title: Medical Travel Insurance for Türkiye: What Standard Travel Insurance Excludes
seoTitle: Medical Travel Insurance for Türkiye: Standard Exclusions
metaDescription: Standard holiday policies exclude elective surgery complications. Learn what specialist medical travel insurance for Türkiye covers before you fly.
quickAnswer: Standard holiday travel insurance almost always excludes elective medical procedures abroad and any complications arising from them, and European EHIC or UK GHIC cards are not valid in Türkiye. Before traveling, you need specialist medical-complication insurance that covers emergency hospitalization, extended recovery stays, re-booked flights, and medical repatriation.
category: Medical Travel to Türkiye — Independent Advisory & Safety (The ITO Standard)

body.text: Does regular holiday insurance cover complications from elective procedures abroad?

No. Regular holiday travel insurance policies routinely exclude planned medical, dental, or cosmetic procedures abroad—and they also exclude emergency treatment caused by complications from those procedures. In addition, the [UK FCDO Turkey health advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health) confirms that the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) and Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) are not valid in Türkiye.

Both the [NHS cosmetic surgery abroad guide](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/advice/cosmetic-surgery-abroad/) and the [Australian Smartraveller medical tourism advisory](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/travel-essentials/travel-health/medical-tourism) warn that failing to disclose a planned procedure can void your entire policy. If you require emergency inpatient care, ICU admission, or medical evacuation after an elective procedure, you or your family will be personally responsible for every bill unless a specialist policy explicitly covers it.
What does specialist medical-complication travel insurance cover?

Specialist medical-complication travel insurance—offered by niche providers such as [Medical Travel Shield](https://www.medicaltravelshield.com/) and [Pulse Insurance](https://pulse-insurance.co.uk/elective-medical-travel-insurance/)—is designed specifically for travelers undergoing planned cosmetic, dental, or elective surgery abroad. Policies typically cover unexpected surgical complications, emergency hospitalization, medical repatriation, and travel disruption caused by a medically required stay extension, subject to policy limits and exclusions.

Even specialist policies do not pay for the planned procedure itself, routine aftercare, or cosmetic dissatisfaction. Always read the full policy wording and declare every pre-existing condition accurately.

body.text: How do you verify emergency hospital backup before surgery?

Before booking an outpatient clinic, confirm in writing which full-service, accredited hospital provides 24/7 emergency and intensive care backup, how transfers are handled, and who pays if admission is required. Standalone clinics without a formal transfer agreement can leave patients scrambling during an emergency.

Check two independent markers: first, verify the facility on the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) authorization list; second, check whether the backup hospital holds international quality accreditation such as [Joint Commission International (JCI)](https://acibademinternational.com/patient-guides/what-jci-accreditation-means-for-patients-in-turkey/), held by major Turkish hospital groups like [Memorial Şişli Hospital](https://www.memorial.com.tr/en/corporate/qualit-management-system). Keep Türkiye's emergency ambulance number—112, as listed by the [UK FCDO](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health)—saved on both your and your companion's phones.
What should your policy cover for extended stays or re-booked flights?

Your medical travel policy should explicitly cover extra hotel nights, companion accommodation, and flight change fees if your surgeon delays your fitness-to-fly clearance. Post-operative swelling, delayed healing, or [blood-clot risk during air travel](https://www.cdc.gov/blood-clots/risk-factors/travel.html) can easily add three to seven unplanned days in Istanbul.
Use this pre-departure insurance checklist before locking in flights:

items: Confirm written coverage for your exact procedure category (cosmetic, dental, hair, orthopedic, or bariatric).
Verify daily hotel limits and whether a traveling companion's extended stay is included.
Check the documentation required for flight re-booking (usually a written hospital fit-to-fly deferral).
Save the insurer's 24/7 international emergency assistance number alongside your policy schedule.

Pair your policy with smart ground planning—starting with our guide to [choosing a recovery hotel in Istanbul](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/recovery-hotel-istanbul) and [questions to ask a Turkish clinic before paying any deposit](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/questions-to-ask-clinic-turkey).

faq.q: Is my European EHIC or UK GHIC valid in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. According to [UK FCDO travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health), EHIC and GHIC cards are not valid in Türkiye, so international visitors must rely on private travel insurance or out-of-pocket funds.

faq.q: Does credit-card travel insurance cover elective surgery abroad?
faq.a: Almost never. Complimentary bank and credit-card travel policies mirror standard holiday cover and exclude elective medical procedures and resulting complications.

faq.q: When should I buy specialist medical travel insurance?
faq.a: Purchase your policy as soon as your procedure date and clinic are confirmed, so cancellation cover and pre-trip protections take effect immediately.

faq.q: Will medical travel insurance pay if I dislike my cosmetic result?
faq.a: No. Specialist policies cover unexpected medical complications and emergencies, not aesthetic dissatisfaction or voluntary revision surgery.

faq.q: Does my Turkish clinic's complication guarantee replace travel insurance?
faq.a: No. A clinic's internal policy rarely covers external hospital ICU bills, extra hotel nights for a companion, re-booked international flights, or medical repatriation home.

faq.q: Can Itinerary of Türkiye sell me a medical travel insurance policy?
faq.a: No. We are an independent flat-fee advisory, not a licensed insurance broker. We help you plan flexible logistics and recovery buffers around the coverage you arrange directly.
